title: Pilot capacity & HC mix — embedded partners pricing probe
content:
Purpose:
Short working sheet for sizing a 90-day embedded partner pilot that combines reserved Dedicated capacity + close SE/Support coverage. Goal: determine headcount mix and pricing levers that yield break-even or acceptable negative margin during pilot, while mapping sensitivity to price and conversion.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
We expect a 3-month pilot with modest volume (median 1.5–3B tokens/month). Baseline plan (6 FTE fully burdened + 4 reserved GPUs) produces ~-$40k monthly operating loss at current price guidance; two realistic levers to push toward neutral are (1) raising effective pilot price by adding integration/SLAs and (2) expanding prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token compute cost. This sheet shows the HC mix, compute allocations, per-month P&L, and a +/− sensitivity grid for price and headcount.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Pilot duration: 90 days (3 months).
- Token volume: baseline 2.0B tokens/month (range low 1.2B, high 3.5B).
- Pricing unit: USD per 1k tokens. Baseline price offered to partner: $0.024 / 1k tokens (pilot discount).
- Compute cost: raw inference cost estimate (fully-burdened infra + amortized GPU + ops) = $0.011 / 1k tokens baseline; savings via caching/quantization can drop to $0.007 / 1k in optimistic case.
- FTE fully burdened monthly cost estimates: Eng = $18k, ML Infra = $20k, Solutions Eng = $16k, PM = $14k, CS = $12k (numbers include benefits/allocations).
- Reserved Dedicated cost (internal): 4 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs per pilot at $6k/GPU/month internal burn = $24k/month. We treat that as fixed capacity cost for modeling.
- Time to ramp for SE/CS is immediate for pilot; engineering ramp assumed 4 weeks.
- Conversion assumptions to paid product after pilot are intentionally optimistic for scenario modeling (see scenarios).

Headcount plan (monthly fully-burdened):
Role | FTEs | monthly cost each | monthly subtotal
Engineering (product/infra) | 2.0 | $18,000 | $36,000
ML Infra / Serving | 1.0 | $20,000 | $20,000
Solutions Eng (integration) | 1.0 | $16,000 | $16,000
Product Manager (pilot ops) | 0.5 | $14,000 | $7,000
Customer Success (post-sales) | 0.5 | $12,000 | $6,000
Total HC monthly cost (baseline) = $85,000
Notes: We budget fractional PM/CS since time commitment is not full-time across the whole org.

Compute & infra monthly cost (baseline):
Reserved GPUs (4 x $6k) = $24,000
Observed third-party cloud egress & storage amortization = $2,500
Tooling / monitoring / logs (pilot retention buckets) = $1,500
Total infra monthly = $28,000

Per-month P&L (baseline numbers):
- Token volume: 2.0B tokens/month = 2,000,000 k-units
- Revenue = 2,000,000 * $0.024 = $48,000
- Compute variable cost = 2,000,000 * $0.011 = $22,000
- Gross margin before HC & fixed infra = $48,000 - $22,000 = $26,000
- Add HC cost = 26,000 - 85,000 = -$59,000
- Subtract reserved GPUs/infra fixed = -59,000 - 28,000 = -$87,000 (monthly loss)
Observation: baseline yields ~-$87k/month. The pilot is expected to run at loss for product validation and conversion pipeline; target is to reduce monthly loss to <$25k via levers below.

Key levers to improve economics (ranked):
1) Price layering: charge for SLA/integration or a fixed monthly seat fee to offset fixed HC/infra. Example: $15k/month minimum commitment reduces loss materially.
2) Caching / prefix reuse: reduce compute variable cost from $0.011/1k to $0.007/1k (saves $8k/mo at baseline volume).
3) Headcount compression: use shared infra-engineering across multiple pilots (allocate 0.5 share instead of 2.0) — requires coordination but can cut HC by 40–60%.
4) Conversion improvement: if paid conversion after pilot is high, amortize CAC across expected paid ARR to justify pilot loss.

Sensitivity grid (monthly result vs price and HC reduction):
Inputs: tokens=2.0B; compute cost=0.011/1k; reserved infra=28k fixed; baseline HC=85k.
- Price −20% (price = $0.0192): revenue = $38.4k => monthly loss ≈ -$96.6k
- Price −10% (price = $0.0216): rev = $43.2k => loss ≈ -$92.8k
- Price baseline (0%): rev = $48k => loss ≈ -$87k
- Price +10% (price = $0.0264): rev = $52.8k => loss ≈ -$82.2k
- Price +25% (price = $0.03): rev = $60k => loss ≈ -$74k

Headcount sharing scenarios (apply HC reduction multipliers):
- Shared HC (baseline -> share factor 0.5 aggregate) => HC cost $42.5k; baseline price => Monthly loss = 48k -22k -42.5k -28k = -$44.5k
- Aggressive share + caching (HC 0.5, compute 0.007/1k): compute cost = 2,000,000 * 0.007 = $14k => Monthly loss = 48k -14k -42.5k -28k = -$36.5k
- Add $15k monthly platform minimum to baseline + aggressive share + caching => revenue = 63k => Monthly P&L = 63k -14k -42.5k -28k = -$21.5k (within target)

Scenarios (3):
1) Baseline (validation-minded): price $0.024, no HC sharing, compute 0.011 => Monthly loss ≈ -$87k.
2) Efficiency path: price $0.024, HC shared 0.5, caching -> compute 0.007 => Monthly loss ≈ -$36.5k.
3) Commercialized pilot (negotiated minimum): price $0.03 + $15k minimum, HC shared + caching => Monthly profit/loss ≈ -$21.5k (still negative but acceptable for ARR pipeline).

Pricing sensitivity vs conversion (brief):
- Estimated conversion rate (pilot -> paid customers) baseline 8% (range 4–15%).
- If conversion reaches 15% and average paid contract size per converted pilot = $150k ARR, the NPV of a pilot supports up to ~$60k one-time pilot subsidy.
- Key: price discounts increase activation but reduce unit revenue; better to keep list price high and offer targeted credits tied to conversion milestones.

Open questions & risks (tracker):
- Q1: Can we offer shared HC across simultaneous pilots without blocking engineering roadmaps? (owner: Anita)
- Q2: Is there a legal / procurement blocker for $15k monthly minimum in partner contract? (owner: Marcus)
- Q3: Can infra team commit to a caching optimization (prefix reuse) inside 6 weeks? (owner: Ethan)
- Risk: Partner volume profile may be bursty; reserved GPUs could be underutilized for long stretches. Consider burst credits or ephemeral pooling.

Recommended next steps (week-by-week):
- Week 0–1: finalize contract draft with $15k floor + overage bands; confirm legal (Marcus).
- Week 1–4: engineering/caching workstream kickoff, target 20–35% compute reduction (Ethan + Sophie).
- Week 1–2: Solutions Eng to produce integration runbook and estimate SE hours (Anita).
- Week 3: Re-run this sheet with measured traffic; update volume assumptions and finalize pilot P&L for exec sign-off.

Action items (owners):
- Anita Patel: produce integration time estimate & 30/60/90 day SE calendar (due 2026-02-20).
- Ethan Morales: draft infra optimization plan + rough ETA and expected cost savings (due 2026-02-26).
- Marcus Hale: start legal template for monthly minimum + termination/usage clauses (due 2026-03-02).
- Priya Menon (owner): coordinate with Finance to map pilot subsidy budget and approve a one-time credit cap (due 2026-03-04).

Appendix: quick sensitivity table (condensed)
- Variables: price change (+/−10%, +/−20%), HC share (1.0, 0.75, 0.5), compute cost (0.011, 0.009, 0.007/1k)
- Short takeaway: meaningful improvement requires combining at least two levers (price floor, HC share, caching). Any single lever alone does not bring pilot close to break-even at 2B tokens/month.

Notes / scratch:
- Consider packaging pilot as "integration + Dedicated reserved" with a time-limited discount that converts to standard list price after 6 months.
- Track token mix: embeddings vs generation — embeddings have different cost profile; adjust compute cost when embedding-heavy.
- If partner can commit to predictable prefix patterns we can claim 30–50% effective token-cost reduction on demo traffic.

Raw numbers and quick formulas (copyable):
- rev = tokens_k * price_per_1k
- compute_cost = tokens_k * compute_cost_per_1k
- monthly_loss = rev - compute_cost - HC_monthly - infra_fixed

End of sheet.
